Let us examine technical RFC 210 regarding database connection scalability and pooling topology. Our direct connection model where 40 microservice instances each maintain 25 database connections caused severe connection thrashing on our primary Postgres instance, exhausting backend memory at 1000 concurrent client connections. This architecture reduces Postgres idle connection memory from 16 gigabytes to 2 gigabytes and supports 8000 concurrent client sessions without database degradation.

In Architectural Decision Record 235, we address data consistency between our primary Postgres datastore and downstream event consumers. Direct dual writes to both Postgres and Apache Kafka frequently resulted in silent message loss or orphaned database state whenever network partitions occurred mid-transaction. We evaluate dual writes with two-phase commit against the transactional outbox pattern.

We standardize on the transactional outbox pattern by writing domain events directly into a dedicated Postgres outbox table within the local database transaction. A separate Debezium connector reads the Postgres write-ahead log via logical decoding and publishes events to Kafka with at-least-once delivery semantics. Downstream consumer services implement idempotent event handlers using Redis deduplication keys with a 24 hour retention window. This design guarantees eventual consistency across 35 downstream services while decoupling transaction latency from Kafka broker availability.

In technical RFC 322, we analyze distributed locking primitives for orchestrating financial settlement reconciliation batches. Our existing optimistic locking on Postgres caused transaction serialization aborts during concurrent settlement runs across 18 regional accounts. We evaluate Redis Redlock against ZooKeeper ephemeral sequential znode leases for distributed mutual exclusion.

Individual product teams managing 22 distinct microservices independently maintained separate GraphQL schemas, forcing client web and mobile applications to execute multiple orchestration queries. We evaluate GraphQL Mesh against Apollo Federation version 2 for unified schema composition.

This eliminates schema stitching maintenance overhead while providing frontend developers with a single unified GraphQL endpoint.

In Architectural Decision Record 375, we address consumer rebalance latency spikes in our Apache Kafka ingestion cluster. Under the default eager rebalance protocol, whenever a consumer node in our 48 worker consumer group restarted, Kafka revoked all partitions across the entire group, causing processing stalls lasting up to 90 seconds. We evaluate static consumer membership against the cooperative sticky assignor protocol.

We adopt the cooperative sticky assignor protocol across all Kafka consumers processing telemetry partitions. Cooperative rebalancing performs incremental partition reassignments without revoking unaffected partitions, allowing healthy consumers to continue processing incoming event batches without interruption. Furthermore, we configure static consumer group membership with a session timeout of 45 seconds so that transient rolling pod deployments do not trigger partition rebalances. In production benchmarks across 120 partition topics, maximum rebalance pause times dropped from 90 seconds down to 400 milliseconds.
